decisions.reason: The input value space was specified as R, but the symbols E_p and z_p used for input parents had no explicit input-label definition. Added distinct in_i labels with E_in_i=R and z_in_i=x_i. The original phrase input or an operation with index less than j already restricts the inequality to operation indices; no ordering of input coordinate numbers is needed. This is a nonfatal notation/interface defect, not a change to the graph class, derivatives, strict-branch rules or choice requirements.

The separate proved result thm-forward-mode-computes-directional-derivative depends on this algorithm and proves Df(x)v. Its Proof 1.1 initializes coordinate derivatives, 2.1 proves the tangent identity at every node by topological induction and the chain rule, and 3.1 covers both operation and input-coordinate outputs. The algorithm specifies DOMAIN_ERROR and NONDIFFERENTIABLE, including ambiguous branches. The asserted absence of a correctness theorem is false; no circular deps or new well-definedness supplier is needed.

The Statement already restricts its open-domain and C1 conclusions to each fixed strict branch, and Proof 1.1 constructs open preimages, 2.1 propagates continuous derivatives by the chain rule, and 3.1 excludes boundary derivatives. Those claims are sound, including empty parents, zero-dimensional spaces and input-coordinate outputs. The former display title could suggest a C1 conclusion on the whole piecewise primal domain; changed only the title to state the existing strict-branch qualification. This is a nonfatal title defect, with unchanged Statement and proof.

A piecewise C2 primitive may have overlapping open branch regions, so ambiguous selection can occur without a boundary. The graph and forward procedure reject that case, but the Hessian-vector procedure only explicitly named boundaries. Made the existing forward invocation explicit, retained its tape and all tangents, and propagated both DOMAIN_ERROR and NONDIFFERENTIABLE immediately before reverse evaluation. Its successful recurrence, zero/one output seed and repeated-slot additions are unchanged. This is a nonfatal omitted status clause; the initial forward recurrence already used the stricter supplier convention.

The title asserted that finite and implicit sensitivities differ, although equality is possible when delta_0=d_0=0. Changed only that title to describe the proved error bounds and residual limitation. The Statement and proof are sound: contraction gives delta_k<=q^k delta_0; subtracting e_(k+1)=A_k e_k+B_k and s_*=A_*s_*+B_* yields D_(k+1)<=qD_k+C delta_0 q^k and the finite convolution K q^(K-1). The q=0,K=1 convention and zero block dimensions are handled explicitly. The qz+(1-q)theta example proves possible discrepancy at zero residual, not universal inequality. This is a nonfatal title defect.

The cited forward-mode theorem explicitly proves the internal-node identity in its Proof 2.1: finite topological induction proves the tangent equals the directional derivative at every node. F3 uses that proved intermediate conclusion, even though the supplier Statement highlights only the scalar output. It therefore does not assume an unproved stronger fact. Differentiating each reverse contribution A^T bar_z by the product rule gives A^T dot_bar_z+(DA[dot_z_pa])^T bar_z; reverse induction yields D(grad f)(x)v. C2 regularity, repeated slots, zero directions, empty parents and the input-output zero Hessian case are covered. The supplier status clarification changes no successful strict-branch execution.

The actual operationwise model named by F2 explicitly requires binary round-to-nearest, ties-to-even, on zero or normal exact results; it is stronger than the published relative-error-only model. A representable normal result is its own unique nearest value. At A(0)=I, triangular primal/basis solves involve only 0,1,2; c=(1,1)^T gives dot products 1+0 and 0+1, and the outer product has entries 1 or 2 before exact sign changes. Thus every in-range operation is exact and the A_theta=(e_1 e_2^T) contraction returns -1. The positive gamma_2 allowance is an upper bound, not a claim of nonzero error. Steps 1.1-3.1 also directly give J(theta)=3-theta and its adjoint derivative. The asserted missing exact-rounding interface is false.

The final sentence gave A(0), B and xhat but omitted the parameterized A, objective and incoming cotangent, so those data alone could not determine -1. Added the full triangular A(theta), b, J=(1,1)x, c=(1,1)^T and the direct nearest-rounding supplier. Triangular solves at zero, identity transpose dots and the outer product use only 0,+/-1,+/-2; normal representable exact results round to themselves. The matrix cotangent is -[[2,1],[2,1]], whose Frobenius pairing with A_prime(0)=[[0,1],[0,0]] is -1. Kept the caveat that d=rho=0 only removes fixed-map errors, not general rounding allowances. This is a nonfatal missing local specification/citation; the example was true for the intended concrete objective.
